quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (NT dollar figures unless stated): consolidated net revenues $177.9 billion, up 6% sequentially and 10% year-over-year (on a U.S. dollar basis up 2% sequentially and 14% year-over-year); gross margin 19.5% (up 2.4 percentage points sequentially); operating margin 9.9%; net income $14.7 billion; fully diluted EPS $3.24. RECORD ATM (OSAT) revenue $109.7 billion, up 9% sequentially and 24% annually, with test revenues up 13% sequentially and 33% annually; ATM gross margin 26.3% (up 3.7 percentage points sequentially) and ATM operating margin 14.7%. ATM factories in Taiwan ran at or near full capacity, with LEAP and traditional advanced packaging utilization outpacing wirebond; overall ATM utilization was around 80%. Service mix: traditional advanced packaging with LEAP is now more than half of ATM, wirebond less than 1/4, and test reached 19% of ATM in Q4. EMS revenue was flat sequentially at $69 billion, down 8% year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: ATM record revenue $109.7 billion (NT dollars), 24% annually; ATM gross margin 26.3%; consolidated revenue $177.9 billion; diluted EPS $3.24; ATM utilization around 80%

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 recap: in Dr. Wu's keynote, consolidated revenue grew 12% at the holdco level with ATM revenue up 23% (the NT dollar P&L review shows consolidated net revenues improved 8% and the ATM business improved by 20%). LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) services reached $1.6 billion, 13% of ATM revenue, up from $0.6 billion (6% of ATM revenue) in 2024; the general segment grew 13% year-on-year; testing grew 36% year-on-year on expanding turnkey and leading-edge test. Net income rose 25% to $40.7 billion (NT dollars) with fully diluted EPS of $8.89; ATM was 87% of 2025 operating profit, up from 80% in 2024. Capex: machinery $3.4 billion plus $2.1 billion of building/facilities/automation, mainly driven by LEAP services and testing investment.
quarterly_data.figure: LEAP $1.6 billion in 2025 (13% of ATM) vs $0.6 billion in 2024; ATM revenue up 23%; testing up 36%; machinery capex $3.4 billion plus $2.1 billion facilities

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 LEAP guidance: leading-edge assembly/packaging services to DOUBLE from USD 1.6 billion to USD 3.2 billion, roughly 75% from packaging and 25% from testing. This is raised from last quarter's view that $1.6 billion would 'most likely' go to $2.6 billion, on better visibility of factory space. Dr. Wu: 'the demand is far beyond the capacity that we're capable of building' and 'we believe we can achieve $3.2 billion comfortably'; the CFO says demand 'continues to significantly exceed supply' and sees 'further upside if we're not constrained by a lot of the capacity build that we're scrambling at today'. Mix: predominantly OS, with wafer sort on the test side. FULL-PROCESS revenue is expected to TRIPLE in 2026 to about 10% of overall LEAP service revenue, with engagement with multiple customers and meaningful revenue by later in the year; FINAL TEST is expected to be roughly 10% of the test business by the later part of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: LEAP 2026 USD 3.2 billion (double USD 1.6 billion; prior view $2.6 billion); roughly 75% packaging / 25% testing; full process about 10% of LEAP

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance (NT dollar terms, FX assumption USD 1 to NTD 31.4 versus about NTD 30.9 last quarter), described as much stronger than normal seasonality: consolidated revenue to decline only by 5% to 7% QoQ, gross margin down 50 to 100 basis points and operating margin down 100 to 150 basis points; ATM revenue down only low to mid-single-digit percent QoQ with ATM gross margin between 24% to 25% (inside the structural range), the dip due to fewer working days and higher Lunar New Year overtime labor costs; EMS revenue and operating margin similar to first quarter 2025 levels. Full-year 2026: a favorable pricing environment; ATM gross margin to stay within the structural margin range throughout the year, improve every quarter and reach the upper end of the range in the second half; 2026 ATM operating expense percentage declining by near 100 basis points (consolidated 80 basis points); effective tax rate about 18%. Management calls price hikes opportunistic and not part of the structural margin, and does not comment on customer price increases; gold and substrate price increases are handled with customers, with whom ASE has long-term service agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 consolidated revenue decline 5% to 7% QoQ; ATM gross margin between 24% to 25%; ATM GM improving every quarter to the upper end of the structural range in 2H

quarterly_data.signal: CAPEX STEPPING UP: the 2026 plan adds another USD 1.5 billion in machinery on top of 2025's USD 3.4 billion, about 2/3 of it for leading-edge services, with buildings and facilities at a similar level to 2025's USD 2.1 billion. Q4 2025 machinery capex was $733 million ($485 million packaging, $218 million testing, $28 million EMS, $1 million interconnect materials and others) plus $456 million of facilities; 2025 machinery split $2.1 billion packaging, $1.1 billion testing, $139 million EMS. Factory space: ASE is building factories from scratch and also acquiring existing factories from partners with clean rooms already installed ('finding new locations and new factories, it's a bit of a challenge'). Management expects heavy capex to continue, 'maybe not just for this year, next year also', and says leading-edge services are margin and return accretive (ROE/ROIC improving, no numbers given). Taiwan Plus One: Penang is the main non-Taiwan ramp (automotive and potentially robotics), with footprint also being built in Korea and the Philippines.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 machinery capex another USD 1.5 billion on top of USD 3.4 billion (about 2/3 leading-edge); facilities similar to USD 2.1 billion; Q4 2025 machinery $733 million

quarterly_data.signal: Technology roadmap. PANEL: ASE will have a FULLY AUTOMATED 310x310 panel line in production by the end of this year (manual today, which management says 'doesn't count'), for chiplet sizes too large for the 300-millimeter wafer form; a move to 620x620 depends on volume and technology requirements. FULL PROCESS 2.5D is not new for ASE; management frames it as second-source capacity next to the foundry partner ('We're not competing'), with configurations evolving as the HBM and TPU size grows. CPO / SILICON PHOTONICS: ASE is working with its foundry partner and the end customer on the silicon photonics (CPO) part, managing PIC and EIC together or separately across chip-to-chip, chip-to-packaging and chip-to-rack configurations, and expects 'some early volume on the silicon and the CPO part of it'. The EMS subsidiary USI made a fiberoptic acquisition, EugenLight, as part of piecing together early deployment for the future optical road map ('There is no conflict' with ASE), and EMS is extending into AI server, optical and power solutions. The packaging toolbox also includes next-generation power delivery for the VRM.
quarterly_data.figure: fully automated 310x310 panel in production by the end of this year (2026); CPO early volume expected

players.product: OSAT assembly and test for Arm server CPUs

quarterly_data.signal: The general (non-LEAP) segment grew 13% year-on-year in 2025 and is expected to keep growing at a similar pace in 2026 on AI proliferation plus automotive and industrial recovery (IoT, automotive, industrial). Part of the general loading comes from the AI data center (FPGA, microcontroller, power management and switch/router devices), though management cannot fully separate it from general demand. Dr. Wu: 'please remember, we are fully loaded'; the pricing environment is 'friendly', and the fully automated general process could gain share. ASE 'bought 2 factories for Infineon' and is 'buying another factory in Penang for ADI' (most likely to close in Q2 this year), and 'the Infineon loading, the ADI loading, they're also coming to us as part of the acquisition'. The communication / cell phone share stays large, with some possible fluctuation.
quarterly_data.figure: general segment grew 13% in 2025, similar pace expected in 2026; 2 factories bought for Infineon plus a Penang factory for ADI
